# WP-X1c - size, evaluation matching and layout

Status: **done**. All requested acceptance checks pass. Files remain uncommitted. No Git command, Julia execution, model fit, campaign, cluster job, regression/probing run or additional scientific source was used. Browser/layout review remains with Claude, as in the existing README.

## Size and reproducibility

All limits use decimal bytes (stricter than binary MiB). Display copies retain at most **48** uniformly spaced sample indices including endpoints, with **five significant decimal digits**. Each bundle shares a time vector across its variables. Full-resolution float64 integration and R2 checks finish before sampling. All three reference cells retain their full unrounded observations; `live.json` is byte-identical to WP-X1b. Rates and every chosen source CSV row are unchanged. Contract version 2 documents this presentation sampling without changing bundle keys. The cap of 48, below the requested maximum of approximately 200, budgets for rows, live data and the full provenance/check manifest. Sampling can miss between-sample detail; five-digit value rounding alone has relative error at most 5e-5.

## Evaluation source audit

`sideproject_q5_noise_fits.jl` includes the Q4 runner, which includes the Q3 machinery and `run_regression.jl`. Q5 lines 100-102 call `q4_evaluate` for observed training, clean reconstruction and opposite-IC clean generalization. Its clean loader reads `(system, ic, sigma=0, rho=0, realization=1)` and the same cell with `3-ic` for generalization; lines 163-165 check those binaries against `build_trajectory`. The exporter reuses those hash-verified binaries and their entire time vectors, including endpoints, rather than generating another target. `simulate` in `src/simulate/solve.jl` takes `X[1,:]` as u0, spans `[t[1],t[end]]`, saves at the target grid and clamps parameters to the optimizer limit.

`build_reference_optimizer` in `run_regression.jl` sets **abstol=reltol=1e-6**, **clamp_val=10**, **maxiters_solve=1,000,000**, reject_nonfinite=false and divergence_limit=Inf. `simulate` uses **Tsit5**. Python now uses **SciPy RK45 (Dormand-Prince 5(4))**, the available explicit fifth-order embedded Runge-Kutta substitute, at the same tolerances, grid and initial state, with the same parameter clamp. It has different coefficients, adaptive control and interpolation; it is not a Tsit5 implementation. The existing Python safety ceiling of 50,000 RHS calls per target remains, unlike Julia's step limit. The illustrations retain their prior DOP853 settings.

The absolute pass tolerance stays **1e-6 on each of four R2 comparisons**. For every remaining failed cell only, both targets are also integrated with **rtol=atol=1e-7**. Classification (a) is movement above 1e-6 in any of the four scores; (b) is no movement above that tolerance. The primary solver output alone determines the pass gate; tightened output never substitutes a curve. Every remaining failed cell has finite primary and tightened scores. No further cause is assigned.

Field provenance: `cell_id`, `system_id`, `stratum`, `active_idxs`, `params`, `reconstruction_r2_arithmetic`, `reconstruction_r2_variance_weighted`, `generalization_r2_arithmetic` and `generalization_r2_variance_weighted` are existing Q5 aggregation columns in the real selected `q5_units.csv` rows. The exporter preserves the complete row. `t`/`x` originate from existing Q5 path `export` metadata and SHA-verified binaries. `scores`, `tightened_scores`, `max_r2_movement`, `classification` and display settings are presentation-analysis fields in the manifest, not invented fit-record fields. All 13 rate columns continue to compare exactly with `q5_rates.csv`. The observation-gate test still starts from an actual Q5 path record; the swap fixture still starts from actual exported dimension-specific cells.

Of **565** remaining failures, **554** are (a) integrator sensitivity and **11** are (b) stable disagreement. All **710** failed/withheld cells have null curve bundles. Only the **922** passed cells export curves. Matching the evaluation settings does not increase the pass count; no threshold or stored scientific value was changed to compensate. The 145 withheld cells still lack stored scores.

## Layout and verification

- Margin notes flow inline through 1450 px, accounting for the 1000 px wide figures; they also wrap long content. This includes 1280 px. The previous smaller-width rule remains covered.
- The initial growth-only playground is `du/dt = 0.23u`. The model display is capped at twice the maximum absolute target population. A visible clipping notice accompanies clipped/nonfinite models; the mismatch uses the original model values.
- Every Cartesian SVG chart now renders both axis titles, with variable names for time, population, derivative, phase plane and drill-down states. The FROLS chart labels candidate terms and reduction fraction; it uses native HTML text and a shrinking middle bar column, with 45 px term and 90 px value columns, preserving font size at 360 px.
- Existing ten tests plus two new tests pass: **12 passed in 12.21 s**. They check the decimal size budget, full reference observations, sampling/rounding on real observations, classification recomputed from tightened scores, axis-title creation, clipping notices and responsive bar structure, alongside all prior data, swap and strict-reference gates. The Node harness verifies execution/DOM structure, not pixel rendering.
- Strict `check_wisp_explainer_js.py`: **exit 0**, all three reference cells pass; maximum relative coefficient errors are 5.82e-13 (sys0003_ic1_s0.03_r0_n1), 4.39e-14 (sys0001_ic1_s0.01_r0_n1), 1.83e-14 (sys0001_ic1_s0_r0_n1). All three illustration checks pass. Both JavaScript syntax checks exit 0.
- The complete rebuild reproduced the already-tested bytes. No browser rendering test was performed.

```text
python analysis/scripts/explainer/build_wisp_explainer_data.py
python analysis/scripts/explainer/build_wisp_explainer.py
python analysis/scripts/explainer/check_wisp_explainer_js.py
python -m pytest analysis/tests/test_wisp_explainer.py -q -p no:cacheprovider --tb=short
node --check explainer/wisp/src/app.js
node --check explainer/wisp/src/compute.js
```
